risk_reasons: Edits worker/index.ts, a worker boot file on the Railway lane
Adds a server-owned field to the Auto-approval settings contract, an autonomy surface
Changes plan-switch labels and confirm copy on the billing screen
goal: Three owner-facing and operator-facing screens stop contradicting the runtime: the Auto-approval settings headline states whether the account is structurally eligible for the Auto-approval lane to post, the billing plan-switch labels name the true tier direction, and the worker boot log names every autonomy flag.
non_goals: Changing whether any draft posts — every change is read-path, presentation, or logging
Clearing the auto_approval_policies threshold inside the tier-downgrade transaction
Adding the new posting fact to the shared AutoApprovalReadiness type or the Admin API contract
Changing TIER_CONFIG prices, Stripe Prices, or any proration behavior
Building a flag registry with a ci: audit that keeps the boot summary complete
Reworking the ReadinessNotices block, which keeps owning expansion readiness
Reading fleet-wide Judge HEALTH on the settings page — three scans per render for a transient answer; the headline reports structural facts only
user_visible_behavior: An armed account default with a Copilot tier shows a banner-attn headline saying the setting is saved but no reply posts automatically, with the tier reason on its own line, and keeps the Turn off auto-posting action
An armed account default with AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED=false shows the same banner-attn headline with the runtime reason
An armed account default with JUDGE_ENABLED=false shows the same banner-attn headline with the judge reason
An armed account default with an Autopilot tier, AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE=false and the runtime flag on keeps the blue headline saying replies post automatically
A suspended account default keeps the red suspended headline ahead of every other state
An account whose account default is off but which has posting location overrides shows the banner-attn headline instead of claiming those locations post, when posting is structurally blocked
The billing plan-switch card labels the higher-autonomy tier Upgrade and the lower-autonomy tier Downgrade, derived from tier order rather than price
A grandfathered account no longer sees both tiers labelled Downgrade, or every tier labelled Upgrade
The tier-change confirm modal, on a move to a lower-autonomy tier, adds that replies stop posting on their own and every reply waits for owner approval from the moment the plan changes
The worker boot emits one structured createWorkerLogger line whose data object carries eleven named flag booleans, including all five autonomy flags and both solicitation flags
invariants: Invariant 3 — no unapproved posting: nothing in this change alters evaluateAutoApprovalCandidate or any posting precondition

Invariant 13 — feature flags stay server-authoritative: the new posting fact is computed on the server and reaches the browser only through the settings API response; no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion is added
Invariant 12 — entry points orchestrate: worker/index.ts only logs the summary; a separate module builds it and owns the flag list
Invariant 15 — domain modules receive their DB client as an explicit parameter
The shared AutoApprovalReadiness type and its blockReasons union are unchanged, so docs/admin-api/admin-api.d.ts and ci:admin-contract do not move
AutoApprovalReadiness stays an expansion predicate; the new field is the posting predicate and the two never merge
No string literal for a subscription tier: tier order has exactly one owner in src/lib/accounts/tier-config.ts
isDowngrade stays presentation-only and is never posted to the tier-change route
Invariant 3's Judge clause is mirrored on the screen: JUDGE_ENABLED=false is a Posting block, because the publisher downgrades every unposted auto-policy row when the Judge flag is off
edge_cases: Autopilot tier plus AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE=false plus runtime on: the runtime still posts, so the headline must still say it posts — the new field must not key on autopilot_unavailable
Several posting blocks at once: the headline states the single fact once and every reason gets its own detail line, so no precedence between reasons is needed
Suspended plus a posting block: suspended wins and renders the red banner alone
Account default off with no location overrides and a posting block: the plain off headline still wins, because it is already true
Account default off with posting location overrides and a posting block: the banner-attn headline replaces the claim that those locations post
past_due inside the 7-day grace: checkSubscription with workerType publisher allows it, so no posting block is reported
pending_payment: checkSubscription denies the publisher, so publisher_subscription_denied is reported
Current tier equals the card tier: the card is the current plan and gets no Upgrade or Downgrade verb at all
accountData.subscription.tier is not a launch tier: currentTier is null, the existing unavailable note renders, and no direction is computed
Two tiers at an equal catalogue price: tier order still yields a direction, so the labels stay correct without a price comparison
A flag env var set to a value other than the literal 'true': readFlag reports false and the boot summary prints false
JUDGE_ENABLED=false with every other gate passing: the publisher downgrades every auto-policy row to owner review (invariant #3), so judge_disabled is a Posting block reason

JUDGE_ENABLED=true with a dead judge sweep: deliberately NOT a Posting block. Judge health is three fleet-wide queries and a transient condition; the headline states structural facts only. Named as a residual gap in the PR

An armed location override with no account default, while posting is blocked: the turn-off action is withheld, because set_account_manual clears only the account default and would leave the override armed
A trialing Autopilot account switching to Copilot: invariant #11 grants a trial full access, so the autonomy warning shows during a trial too
Catalogue prices equal or reversed against autonomy order: tierChangeDirection ignores price entirely, so the labels do not move

rollback_plan: Revert the merge commit. No migration, no env var, no flag flip, and no external contract changes, so a revert restores the previous screens and the previous boot line with no data or state to undo. The Admin API contract is untouched, so the Admin app repo needs no coordinated revert.
observability: The worker boot log line itself is the new operator signal: one structured record per boot naming eleven flag booleans, which is what makes a staging or production autonomy flip verifiable from the logs
